newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skandia seen disposing AFS without Stadshypotek.
newsitem.headline: Skandia seen disposing AFS without Stadshypotek.

text.p: Swedish insurer Skandia is likely to dispose of AFS in one or two years if the proposed merger with mortgage bank Stadshypotek does not go ahead, analysts said on Friday.
Assurance and Financial Services (AFS), a Skandia unit that deals with unit-linked insurance policies outside the Nordic region, had sales totalling $2 billion in the first nine months of 1996.
"It seems likely that the solution (the end to the merger plans) could bring about a quicker decision on AFS which means that it will become a separate company," said Nordbanken analyst Johan Ekwall.
Until Skandia possibly spins it off, analysts saw AFS activity continuing as usual.
Analysts said a Skandia statement, in connection with the merger proposal, that AFS needs five billion crowns over a five year period in order to finance its growth was an exaggeration.
Instead, analysts saw Skandia likely to fund the activities with internal means. Some analysts said that the amount was given to justify the merger.
"If the strong growth on the whole could be reached I am convinced that the share owners would be really happy to take part in a new issue," said one analyst.
Skandia estimates for synergy effects that would result from a merger with Stadshypotek were also seen as too large.
Many now saw Skandia as cornered, losing investor confidence after a failed bid on Stadshypotek.
The company could, however, again be in favour with investors if it would divest a small part to free up capital, analysts said.
Another long-term solution would be to find a new partner within the Swedish bank and insurance sector, analysts said.
"By Skandia having flaunted itself, chances that something like that would happen are bigger now," an analyst said.
For example, a merger with Stadshypotek would have increased the company's credit rating.
"An advantage (with the merger) was that Skandia would have increased its rating and thereby it would have had a larger distribution network in the U.S.," Ekvall said.
The market is, however, relieved after Handelsbanken's 23 billion crown bid on Stadshypotek on Thursday. A majority believes that the bank will end up the winner of the struggle for Stadshypotek.
"What happens is for the best, also for Skandia," an analyst said, adding that Handelsbanken could reach the largest synergies with Stadshypotek.
Although there would have been certain synergies also for Skandia, analysts expected Skandia to be branded as a financial conglomerate.
Analysts said the share was cheap and that it had an upside of at least 200 crowns. On Friday the share closed down 5.5 at 184.5 after jumping four crowns on Thursday.
